findings.doc_quote: The field sits under [hassette.lifecycle] in hassette.toml and defaults to 30 seconds.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/config/models.py:35 `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10`; models.py:335 `shutdown_timeout_seconds: float = Field(default=SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, gt=0)`. docs/pages/operating/index.md:190 also says 10s.
findings.explanation: The default per-hook shutdown timeout is 10 seconds, not 30.
findings.suggested_fix: The field sits under [hassette.lifecycle] in hassette.toml and defaults to 10 seconds.

findings.doc_quote: Hassette runs each variant in a thread pool via task_bucket.to_thread
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/app/app.py:310-335 `await self.task_bucket.run_in_thread(self.on_initialize_sync)`. src/hassette/task_bucket/task_bucket.py:312 defines `run_in_thread`. A grep for `to_thread` across src/hassette found no TaskBucket method by that name.
findings.explanation: The TaskBucket method is `run_in_thread`. There is no `to_thread` method.
findings.suggested_fix: Hassette runs each variant in a thread pool via task_bucket.run_in_thread, so blocking calls do not stall the event loop.

findings.code_evidence: Bus, Scheduler and Api each set a facade: bus/bus.py:158 `self.sync = self.add_child(BusSyncFacade ...)`, scheduler/scheduler.py:151, api/api.py:262. A grep for `.sync` and `sync =` in src/hassette/state_manager/ and app/app.py found nothing, and app/app.py:160 only has `self.states = self.add_child(StateManager)`.
findings.explanation: StateManager has no `.sync` facade. Only bus, scheduler and api do, so `self.states.sync` would raise AttributeError.
findings.suggested_fix: The .sync facades provide synchronous access from _sync hooks: self.bus.sync, self.scheduler.sync, and self.api.sync. self.states is already synchronous to read.

findings.doc_quote: raises CannotOverrideFinalError ... when the app is first instantiated.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/resources/base.py:47-85 `FinalMeta.__init__` runs the check when the class is created, and raises `CannotOverrideFinalError`.
findings.explanation: The error is raised when the subclass is defined (class creation), not when an instance is made. Line 50 of the same page says 'class load time', which is correct.
findings.suggested_fix: ...raises CannotOverrideFinalError when the class is defined (at class load time).

summary: The page is mostly accurate on hook order, the @final enforcement, the automatic-cleanup claims, and the failed-initialization behavior. Own shutdown hooks are skipped after a failed init (core/app_lifecycle_instances.py:126). The errors are one wrong default (shutdown timeout is 10s, not 30s), one nonexistent API (`states.sync`), one wrong method name (`to_thread`), and one imprecise timing claim (the final-override error fires at class definition, not instantiation). Of these, the `shutdown_timeout_seconds` default and `states.sync` would mislead users most.
